public_body: Everett Committee On Legislative Affairs & Elections
overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: cancellations carry no notice requirement, the March 14 meeting was noticed 48 hours ahead on the city website, and the generalized website claim was not reviewed.

allegations.summary: Committee allegedly failed to give timely notice when it canceled its March 7 meeting and rescheduled it for March 14.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law when it did not post 48 hours’ notice that the March 7 meeting was canceled.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the rescheduled March 14 meeting was not properly noticed in advance.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee properly posted notice for a meeting to be held on March 14 by posting such notice on the city website - the official notice posting location - on March 7, which was 48 hours in advance of the meeting, as required by the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Generalized claim that agendas appear and disappear from the city website, without identifying specific notices.
allegations.key_passage: Complainants must allege violations with a degree of specificity, as our office will not conduct broad audits of public bodies based on generalized allegations.
